newsitem.title: USA: Orange County bankruptcy trial recesses for night.
newsitem.headline: Orange County bankruptcy trial recesses for night.

text.p: Jurors ended their second day of deliberations on Thursday without reaching a verdict in the bankruptcy-related trial of Matthew Raabe, a former assistant treasurer of Orange County, Calif.
The jury of six men and six women deliberated for most of the day in Superior Court in Santa Ana and asked to have some testimony read back before recessing for the night.
The panel was scheduled to continue deliberations on Friday, court officials said.

County prosecutors allege that Raabe helped to divert nearly $90 million in interest earnings owed to cities, schools and special districts that invested in the county-run investment pool before the county descended into bankruptcy.
Orange County filed for bankruptcy in December 1994 after sustaining losses of more than $1.6 billion on risky investments. The county emerged from bankruptcy last June.
Raabe was indicted by a county grand jury in May 1995 on several felony counts, alleging he misappropriated public funds, failed to transfer public funds and made untrue statements in bond documents.
Raabe was one of several Orange County officials to face charges after the bankruptcy.
In April 1995, former Orange County Treasurer Robert Citron pleaded guilty to six felonies for his role in the crisis.
A judge last November ordered him to spend a year in jail and pay a $100,000 fine, but Citron was later assigned to a community work program instead of jail.
Citron has repeatedly claimed that Raabe was the "mastermind" behind the scheme to divert the interest earnings.
Last October, a judge sentenced former Orange County budget director Ronald Rubino to probation for charges stemming from the investment crisis.
